data.content:
Court of Justice of the European Union
The Court of Justice of the European Union is the highest court in the European Union, responsible for ensuring EU law is interpreted and applied uniformly across member states.<SEP>The Court of Justice operates in its judicial capacity and is not subject to oversight by market surveillance authorities under the regulation.<SEP>The Court of Justice of the European Union is the judicial authority that reviews decisions made by the Commission regarding fines and other regulatory measures.<SEP>The Court of Justice of the European Union is the judicial institution responsible for ensuring compliance with EU law and has jurisdiction to review decisions made by the European Commission regarding fines.

Articles 41 to 44
Articles 41 to 44 of Directive (EU) 2016/680 outline conditions related to market surveillance activities for designated authorities.

API
API, or application programming interfaces, are technical means provided for accessing data used in the training and development of high-risk AI systems.<SEP>Application programming interfaces (API) allow for technical means enabling remote access to data sets and documentation related to high-risk AI systems.

Confidentiality Obligations
Confidentiality obligations refer to the legal requirements to protect information obtained by market surveillance authorities under Article 78.

Market Surveillance Authorities' Access
Market surveillance authorities' access refers to the permissions granted to authorities to obtain documentation and data sets for auditing high-risk AI systems under the regulation.

Source Code Access
Source code access is the ability of market surveillance authorities to examine the underlying code of high-risk AI systems when certain conditions are met.

High-Risk AI System Data
High-risk AI system data includes the training, validation, and testing data sets essential for the development and auditing of high-risk AI systems.

Chapter III, Section 2
Chapter III, Section 2 encompasses provisions from both Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 regarding artificial intelligence (AI) systems. This section delineates the specific requirements that high-risk AI systems must fulfill to achieve compliance, emphasizing ethical application and governance. Moreover, it addresses the requirements and standards for safety components of artificial intelligence systems, providing comprehensive guidelines concerning their use and approval. By combining these elements, Chapter III, Section 2 serves as a critical framework ensuring that AI systems not only meet safety and compliance standards but also adhere to ethical considerations in their deployment.

Data and Documentation
Data and documentation refers to the materials provided by AI system providers that market surveillance authorities inspect to ensure compliance with the regulation.

International Organisations
International Organisations are entities established by treaties between multiple countries to engage in activities of mutual interest, often supporting law enforcement and judicial cooperation.<SEP>International Organisations are entities established by treaty and composed of member states, often engaged in cooperative frameworks with the EU on various issues.<SEP>International organisations are entities involved in global cooperation that may implement AI systems under specific regulations in conjunction with the Union.<SEP>International organisations work on AI to facilitate global standards, convergence, and acceptance of AI technologies.<SEP>International Organisations are entities that collaborate with Union institutions and Member States to promote global cooperation on standards and regulations.

Authorized Representatives
Authorized representatives act on behalf of providers not established in the Union, ensuring compliance with regulations.

Military AI Systems
Military AI systems are those designed for use in defense or national security contexts, and are exempt from certain regulations.

Recital 24
Recital 24 refers to a specific section of the Regulation that outlines the non-application of the law to certain military or national security-related AI systems.

Recital 22
Recital 22 pertains to the clauses defining the relationship between international organizations and the Union regarding the use of AI systems under specific conditions.

Directive 2002/58/EC
Directive 2002/58/EC addresses privacy and electronic communications, relevant to the protection of data in connection with AI systems.<SEP>Directive 2002/58/EC focuses on the privacy and electronic communications within the EU.<SEP>Directive 2002/58/EC aims to safeguard private life and confidentiality in electronic communications, including data storage and access from terminal equipment.<SEP>Directive 2002/58/EC pertains to personal data processing and privacy in electronic communications.<SEP>Directive 2002/58/EC pertains to the processing of personal data and privacy in the electronic communications sector.

Chapter II
Chapter II of the Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 outlines the liability of providers of intermediary services related to AI systems.<SEP>Chapter II of the Regulation complements the first chapter by providing further detailed regulations applying from a specified date.

Workers
Workers are individuals employed who have rights to be informed and consulted about high-risk AI systems and other workplace issues arising under Union or national law.<SEP>Workers refer to individuals employed and engaged in professions that may be impacted by regulations concerning the use of AI systems in their workplace.

Consumer Protection Regulations
Consumer Protection Regulations are legal provisions designed to ensure the safety and rights of consumers in relation to products and services, including AI technologies.

Transparency Requirements
Transparency requirements dictate that high-risk AI systems must provide clear information about their operations, limitations, and intended uses to ensure informed decision-making.

Human Oversight Measures
Human oversight measures are protocols established to monitor high-risk AI systems' operations to ensure they adhere to safety and ethical standards.<SEP>Human oversight measures refer to protocols that ensure human involvement in the operation of high-risk AI systems to mitigate risks.<SEP>Human oversight measures involve technical implementations that ensure human operators can interpret high-risk AI system outputs and manage their use.<SEP>Human oversight measures entail specific protocols and actions designed to guide natural persons in their roles concerning AI systems.

Target Deployers
Target deployers are the individuals or organizations intended to utilize the AI system, who must understand the instructions for correct usage.

Documentation
A formal record provided by AI model providers detailing the capabilities and usage of their AI models, essential for regulatory compliance and transparency.<SEP>Documentation includes all written materials and guidelines that accompany the AI system, ensuring users understand its proper use and limitations.

Directive 2014/31/EU
Directive 2014/31/EU is a law that pertains to the harmonisation of standards for non-automatic weighing instruments within the EU.

Directive 2014/32/EU
Directive 2014/32/EU is a regulation that deals with the harmonisation of laws related to measuring instruments in the EU.<SEP>Directive 2014/32/EU relates to the harmonisation of laws concerning measuring instruments in the EU.

metrology and benchmarking authorities
Metrology and benchmarking authorities are stakeholders involved in the development of measurement standards and methodologies for AI systems.

Union Law on Legal Metrology
Union Law on Legal Metrology encompasses regulations and directives that ensure the accuracy and reliability of measurements related to commercial transactions within the EU.

State of the Art
The state of the art refers to the most advanced level of development achieved in a particular field, especially concerning technological capability and standards.

Directive on Non-Automatic Weighing Instruments
This directive pertains to regulations on non-automatic weighing instruments, aiming to ensure consistent standards across member states.

Non-Automatic Weighing Instruments Directive
The Non-Automatic Weighing Instruments Directive aims to regulate the making available on the market of non-automatic weighing instruments across EU member states.

OJ L 96, 29.3.2014, p. 107
OJ L 96, 29.3.2014, p. 107 is the official journal reference where the directive related to non-automatic weighing instruments was published, indicating its formal adoption.

OJ L 096 29.3.2014, p. 149
OJ L 096 29.3.2014, p. 149 is the official journal reference for the Directive 2014/32/EU, confirming its legislative status and provisions.

Member States of the EU
Member States of the EU refers to the individual countries that are part of the European Union, obliged to comply with EU directives and regulations.

Data Sets
Data sets are collections of related data used for training, validation, and testing AI systems, essential for ensuring their performance and compliance with regulations.<SEP>Data sets refer to collections of data used for training or testing AI systems, which should be complete and free of errors.

Bias
Bias refers to systematic deviations in data that can lead to unfair outcomes in AI systems, particularly impacting certain individuals or groups.<SEP>Bias refers to the systematic favoritism or prejudice that can manifest in machine learning models, potentially leading to unfair treatment of individuals or groups.

Data Protection Law
Data Protection Law refers to legal principles that govern the processing of personal data, aimed at protecting individuals' privacy and data rights.<SEP>Data protection law encompasses legal frameworks that govern how personal data is collected, processed, and stored in order to protect individual privacy rights.<SEP>Data protection law refers to regulations that protect personal data and the rights of individuals, ensuring that information is collected and processed fairly.<SEP>Data protection law encompasses the regulations and practices designed to protect individuals' personal data from misuse, mandating how data can be collected and processed.

Historical Data
Historical data is data collected in the past, which can sometimes introduce biases if it reflects existing societal inequalities or outdated norms.<SEP>Historical data is past information used in data sets for AI training, which may carry biases.

Data Governance
Data governance encompasses the management of data availability, usability, integrity, and security within an organization.

Privacy-Preserving Techniques
Privacy-preserving techniques are methods used to ensure the protection of personal data in AI system development.

Contextual Setting
Contextual setting refers to the broader environment in which AI systems are intended to operate, influencing their design and use.

Behavioral Features
Behavioral features are specific characteristics of users or data that should be included in datasets for effective AI training.

Directive (EU) 2019/1937
Directive (EU) 2019/1937 is a legal framework set by the European Union designed to ensure the protection of whistleblowers reporting infringements of regulations.<SEP>Directive (EU) 2019/1937 is a piece of legislation from the European Parliament aimed at protecting whistleblowers who report infringements of Union law.

persons
Persons in this context refers to individuals acting as whistleblowers who report infringements of Union law and are afforded protection under the directive.

EU Whistleblower Protection Directive
The EU Whistleblower Protection Directive encompasses legislation specifically designed to protect individuals who report breaches of EU law.

2028
The year 2028 is significant for several reports and evaluations the Commission must submit regarding AI practices.

2029
The year 2029 is significant for reports and evaluations the Commission must submit regarding the effectiveness and enforcement of the AI Regulation.

Standardisation Deliverables
Standardisation deliverables are documents developed to support the AI Regulation and guide the implementation of AI practices.<SEP>Standardisation deliverables refer to the documents that outline specific standards and protocols for various technological developments, particularly in AI.

Penalties
Penalties are administrative fines or sanctions imposed on individuals or organizations that violate the regulations established by the EU for different activities.<SEP>Penalties refer to the legal consequences imposed on entities that fail to comply with the provisions of the Regulation.

Voluntary Codes of Conduct
Voluntary Codes of Conduct are guidelines adopted by organizations and companies that aim to ensure ethical practices in the application of AI systems.<SEP>Voluntary Codes of Conduct are guidelines aimed at fostering the ethical application of AI technologies, especially those not classified as high-risk.<SEP>Voluntary Codes of Conduct refer to guidelines created by organizations or states to regulate practices and promote ethical standards, particularly in the context of AI usage and development.

2 August 2028 is a critical date by which the Commission is required to evaluate the AI Office and its effectiveness in regulating AI systems.

Evaluation Reports
Evaluation Reports are documents prepared by the Commission to assess the effectiveness and progress of AI regulations and the AI Office's functions.

European Economic and Social Committee
The European Economic and Social Committee is an advisory body of the EU that will be informed about the enforcement assessments of AI regulations.<SEP>The European Economic and Social Committee is an advisory body that provides opinions on economic and social matters affecting EU policy.

Binding Measures
Binding Measures refer to enforceable regulations that may be adopted to ensure compliance with established AI guidelines and principles.

Risk Levels Evaluation
Risk Levels Evaluation is a process undertaken by regulatory bodies to assess the potential risks associated with different categories of AI systems.

Regulatory Bodies
Regulatory Bodies are organizations or authorities responsible for overseeing compliance with laws and regulations in the field of AI.

August 2031
August 2031 is the deadline by which the Commission is scheduled to conduct an assessment of AI regulation enforcement.

Union Agency
The Union Agency is proposed as an organization aimed at resolving shortcomings in the enforcement structure of regulations.

Governance and Enforcement
Governance and enforcement pertain to the operational frameworks established to ensure adherence to the AI Regulation and its provisions.

February 2025
February 2025 is a specified date by which certain prohibitions of the AI Regulation will already apply regardless of the full effect of the Regulation.

August 2026
August 2026 marks the full implementation date of the provisions of the AI Regulation.

May 2025
May 2025 is the deadline for the readiness of codes of practice to help AI providers demonstrate compliance.

joint activities
Joint activities refer to collaborative efforts undertaken by market surveillance authorities and the Commission to promote compliance and enhance regulation enforcement regarding high-risk categories.

SME
SME stands for Small and Medium Enterprises, which are specifically mentioned in the context of considering size and impact for penalties under the Regulation.

Start-up
Start-ups are newly established businesses that may also be classified as SMEs and are considered in terms of their compliance with the Regulation.

Administrative Fines for Non-compliance
Administrative fines for non-compliance are penalties levied against firms or individuals who do not adhere to the stipulated regulations and practices.

Authorised Representatives
Authorised Representatives are individuals or entities tasked with ensuring compliance with the regulation on behalf of providers.

Total Worldwide Annual Turnover
Total Worldwide Annual Turnover refers to the total earnings that a company generates globally in a financial year, used to determine fines for non-compliance.

Articles 5
Articles 5 refers to a section within a legal framework that outlines specific obligations and penalties for infringements related to regulations.

EUR
EUR is the currency mentioned in reference to administrative fines within the European legal framework.

obligations of providers
Obligations of providers refer to the regulatory requirements outlined in Article 16, specifically concerning compliance and responsibilities for service or product providers.

authorised representatives
Authorised representatives have specific obligations in accordance with Article 22, representing entities in legal and regulatory matters.

importers
Importers are required to comply with obligations set forth in Article 23, relating to the importation and compliance of products within regulatory frameworks.

distributors
Distributors must adhere to the obligations mentioned in Article 24, which involve ensuring compliance of products they distribute.

notified bodies
Notified bodies are organizations designated to assess conformity with regulations for AI systems, ensuring compliance and safety standards.<SEP>Notified bodies must fulfill the requirements and obligations outlined in Article 31, Article 33(1), (3) and (4), or Article 34, acting as compliance verification entities.

administrative fines
Administrative fines are penalties imposed for non-compliance with regulatory obligations, with specified amounts stated in Articles 3, 4, and 5.

Administrative Fine
An administrative fine refers to a financial penalty imposed for regulatory violations, intended to enforce compliance with established laws and regulations.

Union or National Law
Union or national law refers to a set of legal standards and regulations that govern the operation of providers of high-risk AI systems, particularly concerning data protection and governance.<SEP>Union or national law refers to the collective body of laws governing member states, which may include regulations and oversight of administrative fines.<SEP>Union or national law refers to the legal frameworks that regulate the acquisition and use of data, particularly in relation to data protection and AI.

Technical and Organisational Measures
Technical and organisational measures are the safeguards that must be implemented by deployers to ensure the compliance and safety of high-risk AI systems.<SEP>Technical and organisational measures refer to the practices and systems implemented by operators to ensure compliance with regulations and mitigate infringements.

Judicial Proceedings
Judicial proceedings are legal actions taken in courts regarding the administrative fines and related matters.

Organisational Measures
Organisational Measures refer to the structures and procedures that deployers must implement to manage the use of AI systems effectively and safely.<SEP>Organisational measures are internal practices and policies put in place by operators to comply with regulatory standards and manage risks effectively.

Member State Rules
Member State rules refer to the specific legal frameworks established by individual Member States regarding administrative fines and enforcement practices.

Judicial Remedies
Judicial remedies are legal measures and processes available to individuals or entities affected by administrative decisions or infringements.

AI System Regulation
The AI System Regulation defines and aligns the notion of 'AI systems' with international organisations for legal certainty and adaptability to technological advancements.

Machine Learning Approaches
Machine learning approaches within AI systems enable these systems to learn from data and fulfill certain objectives.

Logic and Knowledge-Based Approaches
Logic and knowledge-based approaches enable AI systems to infer from encoded knowledge or symbolic representation.

Autonomy in AI Systems
Autonomy in AI systems refers to their ability to operate with a degree of independence from human intervention.

Key Characteristics of AI Systems
Key characteristics differentiate AI systems from simpler software, including their capacity to learn, reason, and operate with varying levels of autonomy.

Inference
Inference is a core capability of AI systems that allows them to derive outputs or predictions from data, impacting both physical and virtual environments.

Outputs Generated by AI Systems
Outputs generated by AI systems include predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions reflecting various functions performed by the systems.

Rapid Technological Developments
Rapid technological developments refer to the quick advancements in AI capabilities, requiring adaptive regulatory frameworks to ensure relevance and efficacy.

Environments
Environments refer to the various contexts in which AI systems operate, influencing their objectives and outputs.

Outputs
Outputs generated by AI systems include predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions based on inputs and operational objectives.

Objectives
Objectives refer to the specific goals that AI systems strive to achieve, which can differ from their intended purposes in various contexts.

Functions
Functions are the various roles performed by AI systems, which include predictions, content generation, recommendations, and decision-making processes.

Autonomy
Autonomy refers to the level of independence that AI systems possess to perform tasks with minimal human involvement.

Self-Learning Capabilities
Self-learning capabilities enable AI systems to adapt and improve their functions based on experience and data collected after deployment.

Human Involvement
Human involvement refers to the extent to which human operators are necessary for guiding or monitoring AI systems in their operations.

Regulation (EU) 2024/900
Regulation (EU) 2024/900 is a legislative measure that addresses the risks of undue external interference in elections through the use of AI systems.

March 2024
March 2024 signifies the date of the enactment of Regulation (EU) 2024/900, marking it as an important legislative milestone.

Voting Behaviour
Voting behaviour refers to the actions and attitudes of individuals when participating in elections or referenda, often influenced by various external factors, including AI systems.

Right to Vote
The right to vote is a fundamental democratic principle guaranteed by various international and national laws, allowing citizens to participate in decision-making processes.

Annex XII
Annex XII contains additional regulations or provisions that can be amended by the Commission in accordance with Article 97 and evolving circumstances.<SEP>Annex XII outlines further documentation elements that must be included by the providers of AI models to ensure compliance with regulations.

State-of-the-Art Technologies
State-of-the-Art Technologies refer to the advanced techniques and methods employed to ensure compliance with intellectual property and copyright laws.

AI Model Training Summary
AI Model Training Summary refers to the documented process and content used for training AI models, which needs to be detailed for compliance.

Free and Open-Source Licence
A free and open-source licence allows users to access, modify, and distribute AI models, exempting them from certain obligations.<SEP>A legal framework that allows software to be freely used, modified, and shared, promoting open collaboration in development.<SEP>A free and open-source licence permits users to access, modify, distribute, and use software and data, enhancing transparency and innovation.

Compliance with Codes of Practice
Compliance with codes of practice is necessary for AI model providers to demonstrate adherence to regulatory obligations.

Technological Developments
Technological developments refer to advancements that may prompt changes in the regulatory framework set by the Commission.

Regulation (EU) 2019/2144
Regulation (EU) 2019/2144 is a comprehensive legal framework that establishes type-approval requirements for motor vehicles within the European Union, with a strong emphasis on the safety and protection of both occupants and road users. This regulation specifically governs the oversight of high-risk artificial intelligence systems utilized in vehicles, ensuring that such technologies meet robust safety standards. Additionally, Regulation (EU) 2019/2144 is impacted by updates from Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, which enhances its guidelines and requirements. The regulation outlines detailed rules for the type approval and market surveillance of motor vehicles, reinforcing the importance of regulatory compliance and effective governance for vehicle safety in the EU.

Regulation (EC) No 300/2008
Regulation (EC) No 300/2008 establishes common rules for civil aviation security within the European Union, focusing on comprehensive security measures for civil aviation operations. It is a critical regulation in the aviation sector, addressing both general security protocols and specifications for security equipment relevant to aviation safety. This regulation is positioned within a broader context of regulations pertaining to high-risk artificial intelligence (AI) systems, highlighting its importance in the modern landscape of technology and safety. Additionally, Regulation (EC) No 300/2008 has been amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, updating its provisions to enhance aviation security in response to evolving challenges. It repeals previous regulations, thereby streamlining the framework for civil aviation security within the EU.

Regulation (EU) No 167/2013
Regulation (EU) No 167/2013 is a legal instrument adopted by the European Union that governs the approval and market surveillance of agricultural and forestry vehicles. This regulation includes specific provisions for type approval, which are essential for ensuring that these vehicles meet established safety and performance standards. It has been amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, enhancing its framework and provisions.

Additionally, Regulation (EU) No 167/2013 also addresses aspects related to artificial intelligence systems embedded in agricultural machinery. This connection highlights the regulation's role in overseeing not just traditional vehicle safety and compliance, but also the implications of advanced technologies such as AI within the agricultural sector. Thus, Regulation (EU) No 167/2013 serves as a crucial regulatory foundation for the development, approval, and market oversight of modern agricultural and forestry vehicles in the European Union.

Regulation (EU) No 168/2013
Regulation (EU) No 168/2013 addresses the approval and market surveillance of two- or three-wheel vehicles and quadricycles, relevant for AI technologies in transportation.<SEP>Regulation (EU) No 168/2013 concerns the type-approval of two or three-wheel vehicles, relevant for safety concerns associated with AI components in vehicles.<SEP>Regulation (EU) No 168/2013 is a piece of legislation concerning safety components of Artificial Intelligence systems adopted by the European Union.<SEP>Regulation (EU) No 168/2013 pertains to the approval and market surveillance of two- or three-wheel vehicles and quadricycles within the EU.<SEP>Regulation (EU) No 168/2013 establishes rules on the type approval of two- or three-wheel vehicles and is one of the regulations amended by Regulation 2024/1689.

Regulation (EU) 2018/858
Regulation (EU) 2018/858 is a comprehensive legislative framework established by the European Union that sets forth requirements for the type approval of motor vehicles, trailers, and their components. The regulation emphasizes the importance of high-risk artificial intelligence (AI) systems integrated within these vehicles, ensuring that such technologies meet stringent safety and performance standards. It governs both the approval process and market surveillance for motor vehicles and their parts across the EU, thereby reinforcing regulatory compliance and consumer protection.

Furthermore, Regulation (EU) 2018/858 is periodically updated, as seen with the subsequent Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, which reflects ongoing advancements and challenges in automotive technology. The regulation also highlights the EU's commitment to adopting delegated acts concerning AI systems within the automotive sector, thereby ensuring that emerging technologies are effectively managed and regulated. This collaborative and rigorous oversight aims to uphold safety, efficiency, and innovation in the automotive industry.

Regulation (EU) 2018/1139
Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 establishes common aviation safety rules and creates the European Union Aviation Safety Agency. It lays down comprehensive guidelines in civil aviation, amending several previous regulations to enhance safety measures. This regulation is particularly relevant in the context of artificial intelligence (AI) systems utilized in aviation, as it sets out specific safety rules pertaining to the integration and implications of AI in aviation safety components. Furthermore, Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 is referenced within the framework of AI regulation, particularly in Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, and serves as a legislative act that delineates provisions for safety components in AI systems within the European Union.<SEP>Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 sets the European Union's agency for aviation safety and aspects related to aviation safety regulations being revised in the context of AI as per Regulation 2024/1689.

Directive 2014/90/EU
Directive 2014/90/EU is a significant piece of legislation that addresses standards for marine equipment and repeals earlier marine equipment directives. This directive not only focuses on ensuring maritime safety through regulatory measures but also extends its implications to emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI) applications utilized in maritime contexts. It serves as a regulatory framework that encompasses both the specific equipment used at sea and the compliance requirements for AI systems within the maritime industry. Additionally, Directive 2014/90/EU is linked to ongoing amendments under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, highlighting its relevance in the evolving landscape of maritime regulations and safety standards.

Corrective Action
Corrective action refers to measures taken by the provider to ensure that an AI system meets compliance requirements after a non-compliance issue has been raised.

Certificate Validity Periods
Certificate validity periods define the maximum time frame for which the certificates issued for AI systems remain valid before re-assessment is required.

Testing Environment
A Testing Environment is a controlled setting where AI systems can be developed and examined for compliance with legal standards before being brought to market.

Evidence-based Regulatory Learning
Evidence-based Regulatory Learning involves utilizing data and insights gathered from testing AI in the regulatory sandboxes to inform future regulations and policy adjustments.

Stakeholder Organizations
Stakeholder Organizations represent various interests in the AI ecosystem and can participate in the regulatory sandbox to ensure diverse perspectives are considered in the innovation process.

Stakeholder and Civil Society Organisations
Stakeholder and Civil Society Organisations include groups that represent various interests within the AI ecosystem, contributing to discussions and decisions regarding regulations.

Risk Mitigation
Risk Mitigation involves strategies and actions taken to minimize potential risks associated with the development and testing of AI systems.

Regulatory Sandbox
Regulatory Sandbox is a controlled environment where innovations, such as AI systems, can be tested under the supervision of regulatory authorities.

National Standardisation Organisations
National Standardisation Organisations develop and maintain standards that ensure compliance and safety of AI systems in their respective countries.

Real-Time Remote Biometric Identification
Real-time remote biometric identification refers to the immediate process of identifying individuals using their biometric data in public spaces, primarily for law enforcement purposes.

Rights and Freedoms
Rights and freedoms refer to the fundamental rights of individuals, including privacy and the right to assembly, which may be infringed by surveillance technologies.

Technical Inaccuracies
Technical inaccuracies pertain to errors in AI systems that can lead to biased biometric identification results, affecting individuals' rights.

Biased Results
Biased results indicate the outcome of biometric identification systems that may unfairly discriminate against individuals based on characteristics like age, ethnicity, or disabilities.

Union values
Union values represent the core principles and ethical standards that should guide the development of AI, as stated in the Treaty on European Union.

Human-Centric Technology
Human-Centric Technology is a design approach that prioritizes human well-being and ethical considerations in the development of AI.

National Accreditation Body
National Accreditation Bodies are established to carry out assessments and monitoring of conformity assessment bodies, as per Regulation (EC) No 765/2008.

Confidential Information
Confidential Information includes any data obtained by notifying authorities that must be safeguarded according to specified regulations.

Decision-Making Process
The decision-making process involves how Notifying Authorities determine notifications concerning conformity assessment bodies, ensuring impartial evaluations are conducted.

Information Technologies
Information technologies encompass a broad range of technologies used for processing, storage, and communication of information.

Law
Law represents the system of rules and guidelines which are enforced through social institutions to govern behavior.

Supervision

EU Regulation 2018/1725 covers specific rules related to data protection within EU institutions and agencies, including biometric data.

Article 10 of Directive (EU) 2016/680 outlines specific provisions concerning the processing of personal data and biometrics, ensuring compliance with data protection standards.

Article 10(1) of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 lays out additional rules for the processing of personal data within EU institutions, including biometrics.

Testing Plan
A Testing Plan outlines the procedures and criteria for evaluating AI systems prior to their deployment.

Decision
A Decision refers to the ruling made by the market surveillance authority regarding the compliance or challenges related to AI systems.

European Health Data Space
The European Health Data Space aims to promote data sharing in health sectors while ensuring privacy and security for the training of AI algorithms and other digital technologies.

Testing Experimentation Facilities
Testing Experimentation Facilities are environments where high-risk AI systems can be rigorously tested and validated in accordance with regulations.

Data Sharing
Data Sharing refers to the practice of making data available for use across organizations and sectors to promote innovation and facilitate studies, particularly in health and AI.

Relevant Entities
Relevant Entities refers to organizations and individuals that play a crucial role in accessing and utilizing data sets for high-risk AI systems.

High-Quality Data Sets
High-Quality Data Sets are crucial resources required for the training, validation, and testing of AI systems, ensuring their accuracy and reliability.

Institutional Governance
Institutional Governance refers to the framework ensuring ethical oversight and proper management of AI systems and data usage.

Union level
Union level refers to the overarching level at which AI risks are considered and addressed, likely involving multiple member states.

monitoring activities
Monitoring activities are processes undertaken by the AI Office and scientific panel to ensure AI models do not pose risks at the Union level.

investigations
Investigations are follow-up actions triggered by alerts received by the AI Office regarding potential risks from AI models.

Risk-Management Policies
Risk-Management Policies are strategies implemented by providers to identify, assess, and mitigate potential risks associated with AI models throughout their lifecycle.

Enforcement
Enforcement represents the actions taken to ensure compliance with established regulations and laws pertaining to AI systems and their use by Member States.

Support Structures
Support Structures are mechanisms or frameworks that provide assistance and resources to Member States in implementing AI regulations effectively.

Union Technical Documentation Assessment Certificates
Union Technical Documentation Assessment Certificates are certificates issued affirming compliance with technical documentation and quality management standards under EU regulations.

Quality Management System Approvals
Quality Management System Approvals ensure that an organization meets specific quality standards and is authorized for certain assessments and certifications.

Cross-Border Activities
Cross-Border Activities involve conformity assessments or related actions that take place across national boundaries, affecting how organizations operate in different jurisdictions.

Positive Conformity Assessment Results
Positive conformity assessment results indicate that a product meets the required standards and regulations for compliance.

Market Monitoring
Market Monitoring involves oversight activities to ensure compliance with AI regulations and standards in the market.
